correctness.rationale: The source-model stationary wall-force covariance 2Dk^2 exp(-r|t|)/r and harmonic-chain Green-function covariance yield the stated Fourier coefficient. The Poisson-kernel identity gives each exact positive exponential spatial mode with rate-amplitude constraint A=(Dk/gamma)*lambda/(1-lambda^2). The bijection lambda=tanh(theta/2) reduces the two observed covariances to s=sinh(c)cosh(h) and 1+t=cosh(c)cosh(h). Positivity theta_i>0 is equivalent to 0<=h<asinh(2s)/2; t is strictly increasing in h and gives both sharp endpoints. The inverse formulas follow uniquely and one-covariance nonidentifiability has an explicit continuum. The embedded checker passes 42 parameter-pair inversions, rational algebra identities, Fourier quadratures, and an independent finite-50-chain Lyapunov covariance comparison (six distances; max discrepancy approximately 6.72e-13 for the stated example). All limits concern stationary second moments with fixed d before N->infinity; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The exact forward boundary-reset covariance, spatial Fourier/hypergeometric expression and two correlation scales in related active-bath models are existing results and are credited. The assessed claim instead characterizes the complete two-observation image, explicit global inverse, equality/strict edges and minimality under the physical rate-dependent amplitude constraint. Neither the closely inspected original main text and appendices nor the related active Rubin reservoir paper states or establishes this sharp boundary-reset inverse theorem. Standard Prony reconstruction of an unconstrained two-exponential sum normally uses four observations and does not provide this two-observation constrained image. Actual semantically targeted published-record and literature searches yielded no covering result, though unindexed equivalent results remain possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed inverse-source-identification theorem or constrained Prony analysis may already imply the same sharp two-observation image; no universal novelty certification is asserted.

value.rationale: The parameter identification question is naturally motivated by remotely observing hidden nonequilibrium reservoirs through stationary interior lattice velocities. The proof supplies both a minimal two-observable recovery method and the exact nontrivial admissibility domain, including a sharp equal-rate diagnostic and unattainable edge. These are not generic finite computations, ordinary substitutions, or an arbitrarily chosen statistic: C0 is local kinetic fluctuation and C1 its most accessible nearest-neighbor correlation, the first two observables in the physical covariance sequence. Four measurements are generically needed for unconstrained two-exponential Prony inversion; the physical common-diffusivity amplitude relation lowers the exact requirement to two. The claim provides a distinct inverse use of already-known forward correlations, while honestly limiting results to calibrated and noiseless thermodynamic bulk measurements.
